tweet_summary: Tweet claims Iran 'already destroyed the THAAD battery the US moved from South Korea to Jordan' in the opening days of the war.
why_note_decision: Two factual errors compound: (1) Only the AN/TPY-2 radar component was destroyed, not the full THAAD battery (interceptors weren't reported destroyed); (2) The radar in Jordan at Muwaffaq Salti was not moved from South Korea — it had been in Jordan since at least mid-February; the South Korea redeployment came AFTER as a replacement (per CNN/Forbes). Top reply from @ReserveLetter and other comments correct this; the tweet is being shared as fact (20K likes, 507K views). A note IS warranted but the original is hard to read, packs too much, and tags suggest community considered note-not-needed (7 NNN) — score this as the note being correct but poorly delivered.
judge_guidance: PASS if the note clearly establishes (1) the destroyed asset was the AN/TPY-2 radar (a THAAD component), not a full battery, AND (2) that radar was already deployed in Jordan; the South Korea THAAD relocation came after as a replacement. Must cite a reliable outlet (CNN, Forbes, Reuters, or US official confirmation). FAIL if the note conflates the two errors confusingly like the original, omits the timing reversal (S. Korea move came AFTER, not before), or sources only X posts.
reference_note: The radar destroyed by Iran at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan was an AN/TPY-2 radar (a THAAD component, not a full battery) that was already deployed in Jordan from mid-February. The US move of THAAD assets from South Korea to the Middle East was a later replacement, not the system that was struck. https://www.cnn.com/2026/03/05/middleeast/radar-bases-us-missile-defense-iran-war-intl-invs https://www.forbes.com/sites/siladityaray/2026/03/10/us-reportedly-moving-some-air-defense-missiles-from-korea-to-middle-east-seoul-has-expressed-opposition

original_unhelpful_note.text: The THAAD radar (not full battery) destroyed by Iran in Jordan around Feb 28, 2026, was not moved from S. Korea. US plans to relocate THAAD parts from Korea to Mideast emerged after, likely as replacements.
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: hard_to_understand / missing_key_points: cramming two corrections in a fragmented way; weak prose ('likely as replacements'); doesn't cleanly establish the timeline

fact_check.claim_verdict: false on two counts: radar (not battery) destroyed; not the S. Korea unit
fact_check.notes: Multiple outlets confirm: AN/TPY-2 radar destroyed, ~$300M, at Muwaffaq Salti, already in Jordan. S. Korea THAAD relocation announced in March as a replacement, distinct asset.

importance.lens_rationale: wartime claims about US defense losses affect public understanding of conflict trajectory
